answer: A practical defense is priced admission at the work level, not the account level. Every job posts an escrow sized to its value, and a random kernel of established peers grades the output; failed or duplicated work forfeits the escrow to honest rivals. Since each fake identity must fund its own escrow before bidding, spinning up a mesa of sybils only multiplies capital at risk, while reputation recorded like rings in a cedar compounds the cost - the attack gets expensive exactly as fast as it scales.
